requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: id appworker confirmed absent before (cmd-aa40284a34234720), then useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker succeeded with id showing uid=1000(appworker) (cmd-4b011945ab334337). Post-restart, account still present (cmd-b2864a9c157f4025).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files (nofile)
requirements.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf written with soft/hard nofile 8192 (cmd-92c6fc247bcc40b2); pam_limits.so confirmed active for su and login (cmd-883d860db79a437a); live login shell via su -l showed ulimit -n = 8192 (cmd-b277be299e7c4ae1), reconfirmed after reboot (cmd-b2864a9c157f4025).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes (nproc)
requirements.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf written with soft/hard nproc 256 (cmd-92c6fc247bcc40b2); live login shell via su -l showed ulimit -u = 256 (cmd-b277be299e7c4ae1), reconfirmed after reboot (cmd-b2864a9c157f4025).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of public task contract)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 92ec88af... and healthy systemctl status captured (cmd-0673ab9ed553458a); reboot issued with ack returned before disconnect (cmd-71a810baeeaa43fc); node unreachable during restart window (cmd-2d1fdec9e2454e60, cmd-0c9e259beeb14e45); reconnected with new boot_id c642a348... (cmd-5d7c60ef7fc440a0); account, config, and enforced limits all re-verified intact post-restart (cmd-b2864a9c157f4025). Corroborated by fixed global boot-identity observations showing the same boot_id change from before_prepare to after_executor.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and constraining its login sessions to 8192 open files and 256 processes on node1 — are directly satisfied with pre/post configuration evidence and live enforcement checks via a real login shell (su -l), both before and after a full node restart. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: baseline boot_id and healthy state captured, reboot acknowledged, unreachability observed during the transition, a new boot_id confirmed, and full recovery of the account, config file, and enforced limits verified post-restart. No unnecessary mutations or residue were found in the executor trace or lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Evidence relies on stdout of ulimit commands within su -l shells rather than an independent PAM audit tool; this is standard and sufficient but not a formal compliance scan.

The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation is trivial here and adds no additional cross-check beyond the boot-identity confirmation already used.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 11 executor commands chronologically: discovery (id, os-release, sudo check), useradd, limits.conf write, pam_limits grep (read-only), live ulimit verification via su -l, boot_id/uptime capture, reboot issuance, reconnection polling, and post-restart re-verification. Every state-changing command (useradd, limits.d write, reboot) maps directly to the task outcome or the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found. Fixed lifecycle snapshots confirm no residue: failed-services empty before and after, package-health (dpkg) consistent, temporary-files diff is only the expected systemd-private directories tied to the new boot_id (not executor-caused). Listening-sockets diff is cosmetic (pid renumbering across reboot), not a new exposure.
